problem: Typed Goal validators already require application-owned evidence, trusted evaluation time and issuer validation, but the real pretool shadow caller supplied none of them.

options.name: Keep the current diagnostic-only call
options.correctness: Preserves behavior but leaves the real shadow path unable to exercise trusted evidence validation.

options.name: Add one application-composed trusted evidence resolver
options.correctness: Connects existing validators to the real shadow call while preserving legacy selection and shadow-only authority.
options.complexity: Bounded to runtime dependency composition, ingress validation and focused regression tests.
options.migration: Use an explicit empty fail-closed provider until a real evidence authority is composed.
options.rollback: Remove the resolver seam and its shadow-only projection.
options.verification: Focused ingress tests, typed coverage tests and Product Quick.

options.name: Cut over Typed Coverage to execution authority now
options.correctness: Could complete a later authority migration but exceeds 2B1 and mixes Permit/dispatch risk.
options.migration: Requires atomic MatchProof and ExecutionPermit certification.

selected_responsibilities: Application composition owns the resolver and trust roots.
Typed Goal validators remain the sole evidence admissibility authority.
Pretool shadow remains read-only and non-executable.
preserved_hard_invariants: Business Service and transaction authorities are unchanged.
Missing or invalid trust roots fail closed.
cutover_strategy: Introduce the resolver seam, validate its closed-world shape, pass its values into the existing typed coverage validator, and expose only safe ingress metadata in the shadow record. Keep the default composition explicitly empty and issuer-rejecting until a later authority supplies real evidence.
acceptance_claims: Real pretool shadow receives the resolver output.
State values cannot replace the resolver.
Issuer and time absence cannot produce ready typed evidence.
No Permit or dispatch behavior changes.
